They average moderately positive inflation but include one negative month, so I treat the base rate as noisy rather than a stable trend."},{"kind":"math","text":"Prior/update/interval: persistence prior is the six-print BLS reference class from Apr-Sep 2026; call-0019 gives base mean 0.3014509522592375 percent. Interval method uses realized dispersion of the same six change prints: sigma = 0.41217059726119976 from call-0020, so 1.28*sigma = 0.5275783644943357 from call-0021. Applying that around the point gives call-0025 low -0.3261274122350982 and call-0026 high 0.7290293167535732, rounded to -0.33 and 0.73."},{"kind":"text","text":"Level, momentum, and mechanism: September's transformed print was high at 0.6485480245771891, while June was -0.42248165303806484, so the near-term level path is volatile.
